text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Finland to get a new Traffic Minister after Easter as Matti Aura takes over from Tuula Linnainmaa.
- Ministry of environment wants tighter restrictions on building supermarkets outside city centres to avoid unnecessary traffic and pollution.
- Police warns of fortune-tellers who trick vulnerable people into paying money to get rid of curses.
- The supply of flats for rental has fallen and leases have risen compared to last year, Statistics Finland says.
- Finland and Estonia signed bilateral agreement to abolish visa requirements, opening up travel at the start of May.
- The cost of the illegitimate economy is some 25 billion to 50 billion markka, ministry of interior estimates.
- Lethal traffic accidents caused by young drunk drivers under 26 rose over 40 percent last year to 31 from 22, road accident investigators say.
- President Martti Ahtisaari says he hopes Finns feel healthy pride in living in the world's first information society.
- Rebuilds at Neste's and Statoil's Borealis' plastics raw materials plant in Porvoo to offer 700 short-term jobs after Easter.
- Minority cooperative banks opposing tigher cooperation around OKOBANK may lose their right to use the cooperative logo, said OKOBANK CEO Antti Tanskanen.
- Investments among Finland's top 40 companies rose sharply last year -- gross investment rose ten billion to 44 billion -- but they brought only few jobs.
- UPM-Kymmene's Kaukas pulp mill is running with a daily output of over 1,600 tonnes of pulp without problems after 1.8 billion markka rebuilds.
- Half of Finland's small and medium-sized companies feel taxation is a risk, survey shows.
- Scottish star soprano Marie McLaughlin who sang Mozart in a free restaurant concert in Helsinki says she enjoyed the singing though the event was a little odd.
KAUPPALEHTI

- Two of three in investor barometer plan to diversify their portfolios internationally by buying foreign stocks as soon as Europe's planned economic and monetary union starts. Barometer shows expectation of slight rise in share prices.
- Rising bond yields have eaten three billion markka from the value of government bond portfolios.
- Car traders were hit more than others by recession, study shows.
AAMULEHTI
- Finnish St Petersburg consulate troubled by forged names of Finnish firms in Russian visa applications.
- Heavy snow storms disrupted traffic in southern and western parts of Finland on Wednesday.
